1.explanation:
- form/index.md & form/index.en-us.md: Primary documentation for the Form component, showing the useLabelForErrorMessage API and props related to validation labels.  
- form/demo/validate-label-as-name.md: A concrete demo of using the label as the validation field name, illustrating how validation messages tie into the label element.  
- field/index.md: Explains the Field component’s validation logic and how errors are surfaced in FormItems.  
- core/index.md: Outlines core form internals (including getLabel/getErrorMessage resolution) that underlie useLabelForErrorMessage.  
- core/theme/form-element.jsx: The theme file that renders the actual <label htmlFor=...> and ties the id to the error message container. Examining it helps understand why wrapping the label breaks the association.
1.bug_scenario: In the screenshots and code sample, a business‐wrapped FormItem (“BizFormItem”) injects extra DOM (a <span> wrapper with an <Icon>) around the label prop. Because Form’s useLabelForErrorMessage hook (which looks up the native <label> element by htmlFor/id) can no longer find the direct label node, validation error messages are not announced or linked correctly. The user wants to add an errorMessageLabel API so they can explicitly pass the label node for accessibility when the label DOM is customized.
